recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-22147 unless OO later approves a separate Observation.performer Device change or further revises DiagnosticReport performer semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-22147 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. The final OO decision required adding Device to DiagnosticReport.performer and adding guidance that regulated human diagnostic laboratory work likely requires a human performer, while point-of-care, veterinary, drug screen, environmental surveillance, and similar cases can have a device performer without direct human oversight.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git commit a7db1ac95fed19b3fbdb6d0e73111113bd636225 and merged by PR #3430. That commit changed source/diagnosticreport/structuredefinition-DiagnosticReport.xml and diagnosticreport-event-mapping-exceptions.xml, adding Device to DiagnosticReport.performer and inserting the approved guidance.
additional_context: DiagnosticReport and Observation are active approved build resources in source/fhir.ini. The seed's original description questioned both Observation and DiagnosticReport, but the final Jira resolution and May 2024 OO WGM motion scoped the applied change to DiagnosticReport.performer. Nearby Observation requests were retracted or answered with Observation.device/Provenance guidance rather than adding Device to Observation.performer. Later FHIR-49190 added Patient and RelatedPerson support for DiagnosticReport performer/resultInterpreter and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active DiagnosticReport StructureDefinition already includes the FHIR-22147 Device targetProfile and exact approved guidance text, and editing Observation.performer would exceed the final approved scope.

related_jiras.note: A direct request to add Device to Observation.performer was retracted, supporting no Observation source edit for this seed.
A later Observation autoverification question was answered with Provenance guidance rather than Observation.performer Device.
A later applied DiagnosticReport performer/resultInterpreter issue added Patient and RelatedPerson support and is already audited on the combined branch.
